subject: Adding covariate in lgcp in inlabru leads to two identical intercept terms

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: Adding covariate in lgcp in inlabru leads to two identical intercept terms
parts:
Hi,

I am fitting a LGCP model using inlabru. Previously I did not have covariate information but now new data came in and I want to add the covariate information. However, the fitted result does not make sense. Adding the covariate simply just splits the intercept term into two identical intercept terms. Below is the summary for the fitted model:

Components:
  gal: Model types main='linear', group='exchangeable', replicate='iid'
  f: Model types main='spde', group='exchangeable', replicate='iid'
  Intercept: Model types main='linear', group='exchangeable', replicate='iid'
Likelihoods:
  Family: 'cp'
    Data class: 'SpatialPointsDataFrame'
    Predictor: coordinates ~ .
Time used:
    Pre = 1.77, Running = 8.13, Post = 0.867, Total = 10.8 
Fixed effects:
            mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode kld
gal       -5.695 22.356    -49.588   -5.696     38.161 -5.695   0
Intercept -5.694 22.356    -49.587   -5.695     38.162 -5.694   0

Random effects:
  Name   Model
    f SPDE2 model

Model hyperparameters:
                mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant     mode
Range for f 1964.677 936.11    782.396 1754.361   4363.483 1423.286
Stdev for f    0.663   0.12      0.458    0.653      0.927    0.634

Expected number of effective parameters(stdev): 42.76(13.53)
Number of equivalent replicates : 36.18 

Deviance Information Criterion (DIC) ...............: 6244.31
Deviance Information Criterion (DIC, saturated) ....: NaN
Effective number of parameters .....................: 42.17

Watanabe-Akaike information criterion (WAIC) ...: 6256.97
Effective number of parameters .................: 53.93

Marginal log-Likelihood:  -3140.39 
Posterior marginals for the linear predictor and
 the fitted values are computed

Here gal is the continuous covariate and you can see it is basically identical to the intercept term while it clearly should not be. I followed the instruction to fit lgcp with covariate from this vignette: https://rdrr.io/github/fbachl/inlabru/f/vignettes/web/2d_lgcp_covars.Rmd
What is happening here? Is the way of fitting lgcp covariate updated? Thank you very much!

David

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Adding covariate in lgcp in inlabru leads to two identical intercept terms
parts:
Hi Finn,

I have checked the covariate, it is certainly not 1. The code for model definition is provided below:

#normalize covariate
cov_gal$z <- cov_gal$z - mean(cov_gal$z, na.rm = TRUE)

f.gal <- function(x, y) {
  # turn coordinates into SpatialPoints object:
  # with the appropriate coordinate reference system (CRS)
  spp <- SpatialPoints(data.frame(x = x, y = y), proj4string = fm_sp_get_crs(cov_gal))
  proj4string(spp) <- fm_sp_get_crs(cov_gal)
  # Extract elevation values at spp coords, from our elev SpatialGridDataFrame
  v <- over(spp, cov_gal)
  if (any(is.na(v$z))) {
    v$z <- inlabru:::bru_fill_missing(cov_gal, spp, v$z)
  }
  return(v$z)
}

#point pattern
spv <- SpatialPoints(v_acs[,3:4])

#mesh
v_mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = spv, boundary = region,
                       max.edge = c(80, 800), cutoff = 40, max.n.strict = 1300L)

#spde model
v_spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = v_mesh, alpha = 1.5,
                              prior.range = c(2000, 0.975),
                              prior.sigma = c(1.5, 0.5))

#model components
cmp <- coordinates ~ gal(f.gal(x, y), model = "linear") + f(coordinates, model = v_spde) + Intercept(1)
spv <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(spv, data = data.frame(id = rep(1, nrow(as.data.frame(spv)))))

fit <- lgcp(cmp, spv,
            samplers = region,
            domain = list(coordinates = v_mesh),
            options = list(control.inla=list(int.strategy = 'ccd'),
                           control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
                           control.results=list(return.marginals.random = TRUE,
                                                return.marginals.predictor = TRUE),
                           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)))

Thanks,
David

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Adding covariate in lgcp in inlabru leads to two identical intercept terms
parts:
What does coordnames(spy) say? The component definition you show assumes they are x and y. Some bugs that altered the coordinate names internally were fixed a while back, so that may be relevant.

The function approach isn’t needed for this covariate; use gal(cov_gal, model=“linear”, main_layer=“y”) instead (check ?component to see if it’s main_layer or just layer; if the object only has one variable you don’t need to supply the layer information at all), as that calls a similar function internally.

Also check if the data are on the same coordinate system or not.

Finn
